newsitem.title: INDIA: New crop arrivals turn Indian castorseed lower.
newsitem.headline: New crop arrivals turn Indian castorseed lower.

text.p: Castorseed June delivery dropped to 1,208/1,209 rupees per quintal from 1,223/1,224 rupees per quintal as new crop arrivals weighed on a market ripe for a correction, floor sources said.
"Overseas buying remained sluggish while improved new crop arrivals triggered profit-taking by the bull operators," one trader said.
"Actually the market was technically overbought last week and a correction was due," one operator said.
Arrivals of castorseed in the Gujarat region rose today to 40,000/45,000 bags (75 kg each) against a daily average of 25,000/30,000 bags reported last week.

Groundnut oil remained steady at 340/341 rupees per 10 kg on limited arrivals of 60/70 tonnes while physical buying was at a low ebb. Imported palm oil slid a rupee at 277/278 rupees per 10 kg on arrivals of about 2,000 tonnes at Bombay port. Delivery for the last week of March was quoted lower at 276 rupees per 10 kg.
In Rajkot spot groundnut oil fell by 3/4 rupees at 510/512 rupees per 15 kg.
"Market sentiment for edible oils remained subdued on the back of rising new crop arrivals of rapeseed and mustard seed in the producing centres," one miller said.
